title: Hausa
motto: The major Afroasiatic trade language spoken by 80M+ people across West & Central Africa.
description: Discover Hausa with trans-Saharan trade warmth, royal Emirates greetings, and market eloquence.

proverbOfDay.proverb: Komi ya yi nisa, zai dawo kusa.
proverbOfDay.translation: However far a journey or circumstance goes, it will eventually return near.
proverbOfDay.context: A proverb counseling patience, endurance, and knowing that events run full circles.

slangs.example: Sannu da aiki! (Well done with your work!)
Sai an jima, mu kwana lafiya.

cultureTips.title: The Respectful 'Gaisuwa' Salutation
cultureTips.description: In Hausa culture, greetings are comprehensive and cordial, inquiring about health ('lafiya'), family, and work before moving to any business.

cultureTips.title: Trans-Saharan Trade Heritage
cultureTips.description: Hausa has functioned as the primary mercantile language across West and Central Africa from Niger to Cameroon for over seven centuries.

customUnits.title: Unit 1: The Hausa Alphabet and Vowels (Bakaken Da Wasula)
customUnits.subtitle: Consonants, hook letters (ɓ, ɗ, ƙ, ʼy), glottal stop, vowel length, and tonal drills.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Boko Orthography, Hook Letters & Tonal System
lessons.description: Master standard Hausa Latin (Boko) characters, unique hooked consonants, and short vs. long vowel distinctions.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a special hooked consonant (bàƙin ƙirƙira) in the Hausa Boko alphabet?
questions.explanation: Hausa features distinctive implosive and ejective consonants written with hooked letters: Ɓ/ɓ, Ɗ/ɗ, Ƙ/ƙ, and ʼY/ʼy.

questions.prompt: Match the Hausa hooked letter with its phonetic description:
In Hausa, vowel length changes meaning: 'fari' means white, while 'faari' means ___.
questions.sentence: In Hausa, vowel length changes meaning: 'fari' means white, while 'faari' means ___.
questions.explanation: Vowel length is phonemic in Hausa: short vowel 'fari' (white) contrasts with long vowel 'faari' (drought/famine).
